title: Sheaf realization of formal families over a base preserves finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with fibre products, let $J$ be a subcanonical Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $T\in\mathcal C$. For the category of formal families [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], define $R_T:\mathrm{FC}(\mathcal C/T)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)/h_T$ by sending $\{U_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ to the coproduct in the sheaf slice of the representable sheaves $h_{U_i}\to h_T$, with maps induced by the index and component maps. Then $R_T$ preserves finite limits. The coproducts and sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] are taken in the same small universe as the formal index sets.

proof.text: Identify the formal-family Yoneda functor with ordinary Yoneda on formal families restricted along singleton families. A map from a singleton to a family is uniquely an index together with a component arrow. This identifies its presheaf value with the coproduct of representables, naturally in the family and test object. Ordinary Yoneda and restriction of presheaves preserve limits, so the formal-family Yoneda functor preserves limits.

Identify formal families in the slice C/T with the slice of formal families over the singleton {T}: retain the index set and the structural component maps to T. The inverse reads these components as objects of C/T; PUnit uniqueness gives the inverse equations.

Compose this equivalence with the slice functor induced by formal-family Yoneda and sheafification. Yoneda preserves limits and sheafification preserves finite limits. Subcanonicity identifies the sheafification of the singleton representable with h_T. Changing the slice base along this isomorphism also preserves limits.

The composite preserves coproducts and agrees with sheaf Yoneda on singleton families. Every formal family is the coproduct of its singleton families. Its two coproduct universal properties therefore give a natural isomorphism with the explicitly defined realization R_T. Transport finite-limit preservation along that natural isomorphism.
